name: Pravinbhai Patel
current_role: Whole-time Director (long-time Chairman) of Patel Infrastructure Ltd, Vadodara
profile: Pravinbhai Vithalbhai Patel is a second-generation leader of Patel Infrastructure, the Vadodara road, highway, bridge and irrigation contractor founded by his father Vitthalbhai Gobarbhai Patel in 1972. He long served as chairman alongside his brother, MD Arvind Patel; the company has filed for an IPO (Rs 400 cr fresh issue) with SEBI.
interesting_fact: Patel Infrastructure was among the contractors for the first phase of the Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway, and its highway arm won a Silver Award at India's National Highway Awards for Excellence 2018.
notes: Title conflict: older sources (Craft, MarketScreener, CEO Magazine) call him Chairman & Whole-time Director; the current patelinfra.com About page lists brother Arvindbhai as Chairman and Pravin V. Patel as Whole-time Director. A 2015 Volvo CE case study quotes the family on PIPL's 'humble beginnings as a small family business in the 1970s'. Low public profile.

name: Ling Zhenrong
current_role: Director and major shareholder, Sichuan Kexin Mechanical and Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300092)
profile: Lin (Ling) Zhenrong, about 62, is a long-time director and co-owner of Sichuan Kexin Mechanical & Electrical, a Shifang (Deyang), Sichuan maker of Class III pressure vessels for petrochemical, nuclear and new-energy plants, founded 1997 and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext. He sits on the board alongside Lin Zhenhua, the company's chairman and legal representative.
interesting_fact: Kexin is one of the few private Chinese firms licensed to make civil nuclear-safety mechanical equipment, in addition to its pressure-vessel business, a direct link to the energy theme of the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Per MarketScreener, he has also been a director of Sichuan Sunshine Plastics Co. Ltd. since December 2007, alongside his Kexin board seat.
notes: Usually romanized Lin Zhenrong (Zhen Rong Lin); 'Ling' appears to be a list spelling variant. Very low public profile, and there is almost no English-language coverage. The best route is Kexin's board secretary/IR office via its SZSE (cninfo) filings. Chairman/legal rep is Lin Zhenhua.

name: Suresh G Kare
current_role: Chairman, Indoco Remedies Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Suresh Govind Kare is chairman of Indoco Remedies, the Mumbai pharma maker of formulations and APIs founded by his father Govind Ramnath Kare in 1947. He took over the family firm and built it into a profitable, listed drug maker with export plants in Goa; daughter Aditi Kare Panandikar is now MD while he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Indoco was incorporated on 23 August 1947, eight days after Indian independence, by his father to make indigenous medicines, making it one of India's oldest pharma companies.
deep_cut_fact: A past President of the Indian Drug Manufacturers' Association (IDMA), he was felicitated by Amitabh Bachchan at IDMA's Golden Jubilee celebrations in Mumbai in January 2012 for decades of service to the industry.
notes: Sources differ on whether his chairmanship is executive or non-executive. In late 2025 Kare family trusts took over shares from family members. Low media profile; go through Indoco corporate communications.

name: Zhou Tianbao
current_role: Unknown; former founder/CEO of Norstar Founders Group (auto parts, HKEX: 2339)
profile: Zhou Tianbao built Norstar, a Zhejiang auto-components group (shock absorbers and other parts) that grew into one of China's biggest exporters to the US, Canada and Europe and listed in Hong Kong as Norstar Founders Group. Around 2008-09 provisional liquidators were appointed to the listed company, and its shell later became BeijingWest Industries International. His current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: In 2006, as CEO, he set out to pivot an almost entirely export-driven parts maker toward China's booming car market, targeting domestic revenue growth above 30% a year, up from about 12%.
deep_cut_fact: He called China's mainland auto market 'a golden opportunity for us to further boost our sales at home' at a time when nearly all of Norstar's sales came from North American and European exports.
notes: Probably stale wealth listing. Norstar Founders Group went into provisional liquidation around the 2008-09 auto slump amid FX contract losses (SCMP), and the listed shell is now BeijingWest Industries International. No current public role or contact found; whereabouts unknown. Not a good podcast target.

name: Sudarshan Kumar Saraf
current_role: Co-Chairman & Managing Director, Technocraft Industries (India) Ltd, Mumbai
profile: Sudarshan Kumar Saraf co-founded Technocraft with his elder brother Sharad in 1972, starting with borrowed capital on a Mumbai industrial plot. The group grew into one of the world's largest makers of steel drum closures and also makes scaffolding, formwork, textiles and engineering services, with affiliates in Canada, China and Poland. He holds roughly 28% of the listed company.
interesting_fact: Technocraft says it was the first company to break an American multinational's monopoly in drum closures, and became the world's second-largest drum-closure producer.
deep_cut_fact: An IIT Bombay mechanical engineering alumnus, he is a keen alumni organizer: during the class of 1969's silver jubilee in 1994 he helped raise Rs 12 lakh in alumni contributions for the institute.
notes: Engineer-founder. The company profile credits him with pioneering an interval thread-rolling process and building special-purpose machines. Sources differ on his title (Co-Chairman & MD vs Chairman); brother Sharad is generally listed as Chairman. Low media profile.

name: Shobana Kamineni
current_role: Promoter director, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise; proposed Executive Chairperson of Apollo Healthtech (pharmacy and digital-health spin-off, listing targeted FY27)
profile: Shobana Kamineni, daughter of Apollo founder Prathap C. Reddy, built Apollo's pharmacy, Apollo 24/7 digital health and the Apollo Munich insurance businesses. She gave up her Executive Vice Chairperson title at the parent but stays on the board, and in June 2026 Apollo proposed her as executive chair of Apollo Healthtech ahead of its planned standalone listing.
interesting_fact: In 2017-18 she became the first woman president of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in its more than 100-year history.
deep_cut_fact: She championed Apollo's 'Biobank', a catalogued library of ethically consented, anonymized bio-samples, which Time magazine listed among the top 10 life-sciences ideas of the decade. She also founded the heart-health NGO 'Billion Hearts Beating'.
notes: High-profile and well connected (WEF EDISON Alliance board, FIND board). Her Apollo Healthtech chair appointment is subject to shareholder/NCLT approval. No verified personal X account found. Route via Apollo corporate communications or IR.

name: Chen Libin
current_role: Listed as associated with Qiaoyu Group (China); not verified
notes: English and Chinese searches (Qiaoyu Group / 侨宇 / 乔宇 / 桥宇 + 陈立斌/陈利斌) found no verifiable record tying a Chen Libin to a 'Qiaoyu Group'. The Chinese characters are needed to identify him, e.g. from the original rich-list entry, before doing more research.

name: Margot Golden
current_role: Director, The New York Times Company (since 2024); Chair, Ochs-Sulzberger Trust
profile: Margot Golden Tishler, about 49, is a fifth-generation member of the Ochs/Sulzberger family that controls The New York Times Company through its Class B shares. She chairs the family's Ochs-Sulzberger Trust and joined the NYT board in 2024, succeeding her relative Hays N. Golden. Her wealth comes from the family's inherited NYT stake.
interesting_fact: As chair of the Ochs-Sulzberger Trust she sits at the center of the dual-class structure that has kept one family in control of The New York Times since Adolph Ochs bought it in 1896.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the boardroom she is a freelance graphic designer with an associate degree in graphic design from Pratt Institute, and she manages a small company that sells accessories for children's clothing.
notes: Also listed as Margot Golden Tishler. Very private family member with no public media presence. The contacts are NYT's corporate press and IR contacts from the Feb 2024 nomination release and may have changed. Not an obvious fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Steven H Collis
current_role: Board director, Elevance Health and Bausch + Lomb; former Chairman & CEO of Cencora (retired from Cencora's board Sept 30, 2025)
profile: South African-born Steven Collis joined AmerisourceBergen (now Cencora) in the mid-1990s, built its Specialty Group, and was CEO from 2011 to 2024 and then executive chairman until September 2025. He led the 2023 rebrand to Cencora and the company's global expansion. He now serves on the boards of Elevance Health and Bausch + Lomb.
interesting_fact: He received HDA's 2024 Nexus Award for Lifetime Achievement, the US drug-distribution industry's highest individual honor, after nearly three decades at Cencora.
deep_cut_fact: A Johannesburg native and honors graduate of the University of the Witwatersrand, he was a founding Vice Chairman of the American Cancer Society's CEOs Against Cancer Greater Philadelphia chapter.
notes: Now in board/retirement phase, so he may have more time for a podcast. Board bio at https://www.bausch.com/about-bausch-lomb/board/Steven-H-Collis/. He spoke about his upbringing on the Withology podcast (March 2024). No personal channel found; the best route is a mutual contact or the board offices of Elevance or Bausch + Lomb.

name: Stephen B Burke
current_role: Lead Independent Director, JPMorgan Chase; Director, Berkshire Hathaway; Senior Advisor, Comcast
profile: Steve Burke (b. 1958) ran Comcast Cable, then was CEO of NBCUniversal from 2011 to 2019 after the Comcast-GE deal, led the Sky acquisition and set up Peacock before retiring as NBCU chairman in 2020. He is now lead independent director at JPMorgan Chase, a Berkshire Hathaway director, and invests through his family firm Madison Valley Partners (e.g. onX Maps).
interesting_fact: Before Comcast he spent 12 years at Disney. He was president and COO of Euro Disney (1992-96) during its troubled early years, then ran ABC Broadcasting.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as an associate product manager in General Foods' breakfast-food division, then in 1986 joined Disney and founded the Disney Store concept for its consumer-products division.
notes: Official board bio: https://www.jpmorganchase.com/about/our-leadership/stephen-burke. Son of Capital Cities/ABC executive Dan Burke. Became an onX Maps (Missoula, MT) board member and investor in 2021. No personal public channel found; the route is via JPMorgan's corporate secretary or a Comcast/Berkshire connection.

name: Chen Zhangqiao
current_role: Listed as associated with Wuzhou Holding Group (China); not verified
notes: English and Chinese searches (Chen Zhangqiao / 陈章桥 + Wuzhou / 五洲) found no record linking this name to a 'Wuzhou Holding Group'. Hong Kong-listed Wuzhou International Holdings has a different board. The Chinese characters or the city are needed to disambiguate.

name: Eric Andersen
current_role: President & CEO, AIG (since June 1, 2026)
profile: Eric Andersen spent about three decades at Aon, as CEO of Aon Benfield (reinsurance), CEO of Aon Risk Solutions Americas and president of Aon from 2020 to 2025. He joined AIG as CEO-elect in February 2026 and succeeded Peter Zaffino as president and CEO on June 1, 2026, also joining AIG's board.
interesting_fact: He moved from the broker side (Aon) to run one of the world's largest insurers, an unusual crossover. Zaffino, his predecessor, had made a similar jump from Marsh/Guy Carpenter.
deep_cut_fact: A Colgate political-science graduate with a Fordham MBA, he serves on Colgate's Board of Trustees and on the board of Covenant House New Jersey, which serves young people facing homelessness.
notes: Newly installed CEO of a large insurer. Insuring data centers and energy transition risk is a possible podcast angle. Business Roundtable member. Route via AIG media relations.

name: Barry Eggers
current_role: Founding Partner, Lightspeed Venture Partners (Menlo Park)
profile: Barry Eggers co-founded Lightspeed Venture Partners after six years at Cisco and focuses on enterprise infrastructure and cybersecurity. Lightspeed was an early lead investor in Rubrik (IPO 2024, ~24% stake) and Netskope (first backed with a $21M Series B in 2013, IPO 2025), and Eggers is reported as a 10% owner of both through Lightspeed vehicles. He also backed Nutanix early.
interesting_fact: Netskope's 2025 IPO followed Rubrik's in 2024. These were two rare cybersecurity IPOs, and Lightspeed was a top holder in both (about 19% of Netskope and about 24% of Rubrik at listing).
deep_cut_fact: At Cisco (1991-97), before co-founding Lightspeed, he built major sales channels and set up the company's first mergers-and-acquisitions process. He holds a UCLA BA in economics/business and a Stanford MBA.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center/infrastructure podcast (enterprise infra and storage investor). Advisory member of The Nature Conservancy's Investment Committee. He and his wife fund conservation, sustainability and mentoring initiatives. Best route is via Lightspeed's comms team.

name: Mission Sponsor Aa Ii
current_role: Not a person: SPAC sponsor entity (10% owner) of AA Mission Acquisition Corp. II (NYSE: YCY)
profile: 'Mission Sponsor AA II' is the sponsor vehicle of AA Mission Acquisition Corp. II, a Cayman Islands blank-check company based in The Woodlands, Texas. It raised $115M (incl. over-allotment) in an October 2025 NYSE IPO to target food and beverage businesses valued at $200M-$1B. The sponsor team is led by Chairman/CEO Qing Sun and CFO Shibin Fang.
interesting_fact: The same team's first SPAC, AA Mission Acquisition Corp. (AAMU), listed in August 2024 and was still seeking a target when SPAC II priced.
notes: Entity, not an individual, so drop it from person outreach. If relevant, the human behind it is Qing Sun (Chairman/CEO). The SPAC's contact details are in its SEC filings and IPO press releases on Business Wire (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251002720177/en).

name: Colin Walsh
current_role: Managing Director, Life Sciences Investing, Goldman Sachs Alternatives; Director, Attovia Therapeutics (Nasdaq: ATTO)
profile: Colin Walsh, Ph.D., is a biotech investor. He was a partner at Qiming Venture Partners USA from 2019, then joined Goldman Sachs as an MD in life sciences investing in 2023. He joined Attovia's board when Goldman Sachs Alternatives led its $105M Series B, and sits or has sat on the boards of Ceptur, Vicebio, Korro Bio and Element Science. His insider status at Attovia reflects Goldman fund holdings.
interesting_fact: He came to investing from the lab: his Ph.D. in the joint UC Berkeley-UCSF bioengineering program focused on novel delivery systems for RNA therapeutics, funded by an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his undergraduate degree at UMass Amherst and a Management of Technology certificate from Berkeley Haas. In 2020 he was promoted from principal to partner at Qiming US, the independent US healthcare fund affiliated with China's Qiming Venture Partners.
notes: Common name, so check you have the right Colin Walsh (biotech investor at Goldman Sachs, not others with the same name). Likely not UHNW himself; the insider status comes from fund-held shares. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Route via Goldman Sachs Alternatives media relations.

name: Chung Han Hsieh
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Chief Technology Officer, OBOOK Holdings / OwlTing Group (Nasdaq: OWLS), Taipei
profile: Chung-Han 'John' Hsieh, 45, co-founded OwlTing in Taipei in 2010 with CEO Darren Wang and has been CTO since. The company started with the OwlTing Market food e-commerce platform and grew into a blockchain/fintech group (OwlPay stablecoin payments, OwlNest hospitality software) that listed on Nasdaq in 2025. He holds about 11.5% of the shares.
interesting_fact: OwlTing now holds US money-transmitter licenses covering 42 states and in 2026 launched an 'OwlPay Agent Wallet' for AI-agent (agentic) commerce.
deep_cut_fact: Before OwlTing he was CTO of LGS (TaiwanGo) from 2004 to 2010, and his bachelor's degree from National Taiwan University is in bio-industrial mechatronics, not computer science.
notes: Goes by John Hsieh. A technical co-founder, so a good fit for a stablecoin/AI-payments infrastructure conversation. CEO Darren Wang is the public face of the company.

name: Micheal G. Dunn
current_role: Retired (May 2025); former EVP & Chief Operating Officer, The Williams Companies (2017-2025)
profile: Micheal Dunn is a civil engineer and long-time natural-gas pipeline executive. He was president of Kern River Gas Transmission, president and CEO of PacifiCorp Energy (Berkshire Hathaway Energy) from 2010 to 2015, and president of Questar Pipeline. He then served as Williams' first COO from 2017, overseeing projects such as Transco's Regional Energy Access expansion, and retired in May 2025.
interesting_fact: He ran PacifiCorp Energy, Berkshire Hathaway Energy's regulated power-generation arm, for five years before going back to gas pipelines at Questar and Williams. That gives him unusual experience on both the power and the gas side of the US energy system.
deep_cut_fact: His career came full circle: he started at Williams as an operations engineer, joined Kern River in 1990 and rose to president, then returned to Williams decades later as COO. He earned his University of Oklahoma civil engineering degree in 1988 and is a registered PE in Oklahoma.
notes: Spelled 'Micheal' (not Michael). Now retired, so he may be open to a podcast about gas pipelines feeding data-center load growth. No public personal channel found; best via Williams corporate communications or industry networks (INGAA, Tulsa).

name: Scott A Hudson
current_role: EVP & President, Vistra Retail (incl. President of TXU Energy), Vistra Corp.
profile: Scott Hudson runs Vistra's retail electricity business, including TXU Energy, Texas's largest competitive power retailer. He joined TXU Energy in 2011 as COO and became its president, and he now leads all of Vistra's retail brands. Earlier he held senior roles at MBNA America, ChoicePoint and LexisNexis.
interesting_fact: His Vistra Retail unit sits inside one of the biggest beneficiaries of data-center power demand: in January 2026 Vistra signed agreements with Meta to support its PJM nuclear plants and add new nuclear generation. He also chairs the Retail Energy Advancement League.
deep_cut_fact: A Yale graduate with a UNC-Chapel Hill law degree, he began his career as a commercial energy lawyer at Troutman Sanders before moving into consumer businesses. He also sits on the board of the Dallas Children's Theatre.
notes: Good energy-podcast fit (retail power, residential batteries and VPPs, e.g. Vistra's 2026 Enphase battery aggregation expansion). Sources disagree on exact title dates (TXU president since 2011 vs 2017). Route via Vistra media relations.

name: William F. Gifford Jr.
current_role: Former CEO of Altria Group (stepped down after the May 14, 2026 annual meeting; consultant through end-2026)
profile: Billy Gifford joined Philip Morris USA in 1994 and rose through finance, strategy and consumer research to become Altria's CFO (2015-18), vice chairman, and CEO from April 2020. As CEO he steered the Marlboro maker toward smoke-free products (NJOY, on! nicotine pouches). He handed the CEO role to CFO Sal Mancuso in May 2026 and is staying on as a consultant through 2026.
interesting_fact: He spent his entire 30-plus-year corporate career inside the Philip Morris/Altria system, rising from staff accountant to CEO of the Fortune 500 company.
deep_cut_fact: A VCU business/accounting graduate, he started as an auditor at Coopers & Lybrand in Richmond before joining Philip Morris USA in 1994 as an accountant. He has served as a trustee of the VCU School of Business Foundation.
notes: Recently retired as CEO. Tobacco is a sensitive topic and a weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. No personal public channel found; route via Altria media relations or a Richmond business network. Board seats are inconsistent across sources (AB InBev, Catalyst), so verify before mentioning them.

name: H Eric Bolton Jr
current_role: Executive Chairman, MAA (Mid-America Apartment Communities); Director, EastGroup Properties
profile: Eric Bolton joined Memphis-based apartment REIT MAA in 1994 and was CEO from 2001 to March 2025 (chairman since 2002). Over that time he built it into one of the largest Sun Belt multifamily owners, including the 2016 merger with Post Properties. Brad Hill succeeded him as CEO in April 2025, and he now serves as executive chairman under an agreement running through 2026. He has been an EastGroup director since 2013.
interesting_fact: He ran MAA as CEO for 23 years (2001-2025), one of the longest CEO tenures among US REITs, and spent more than 30 years with the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before MAA he spent seven years at Trammell Crow in Dallas, ending as EVP/CFO of Trammell Crow Asset Management. He holds an accounting BBA from the University of Memphis and a finance and real estate MBA from the University of North Texas.
notes: Transitioning out (executive chairman agreement ends Dec 31, 2026), so he may have more time. Real estate rather than energy, but Sun Belt population and job growth links to the data-center build-out. Route via MAA IR.
